# Job Chapter 22 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 424r–424v

---

**22:1** And-answered Elifaz [Eliphaz] the-Temanite and-said:

**22:2** "Can-a-man [ha-le-el] be-profitable [yiskon] to-God [gever]? For [ki] to-himself the-wise-one [maskil] is-profitable [yiskon]. **22:3** [Is it] a-delight [ha-chefets] to-Shaddai that you-are-righteous [ki titsdaq]? Or a-gain [betsa'] that you-make-your-ways-blameless [ki tatim derakhekha]?

**22:4** Is-it for-your-fear [ha-miyir'atekha] [that] he-rebukes-you [yokhichekha], [that] he-enters [yavo] with-you into-judgment [bamishpat]?

**22:5** Is-not your-evil [ra'atekha] great [rabbah]? And-there-is-no end [ein qets] to-your-iniquities [la'avonotekha].

**22:6** For you-have-taken-pledges [tachbol] from-your-brothers [achekha] for-nothing [chinnam], and-the-clothing [bigdei] of-the-naked [arummim] you-strip [tafshit]. **22:7** You-do-not give-water [tasqeh] to-the-weary [ayyef], and-from-the-hungry [vera'ev] you-withhold [timna'] bread [lachem].

**22:8** And-the-man of-arm [uish zeroa'] — to-him [is] the-land [ha-arets]; and-the-one-lifted-in-face [une-su fanim] dwells [yeshev] in-it. **22:9** Widows [almanot] you-have-sent-away [shillachta] empty [reiqam], and-the-arms [uzrot] of-orphans [yetomim] are-crushed [yedukkah].

**22:10** Therefore snares [pachim] [are] all-around-you [sevivotekha], and-sudden fear [pachad pit'om] terrifies-you [vivahalkha]; **22:11** or darkness [choshekh] [so that] you-cannot see [lo tireh], and-a-flood [shif'at] of-waters [mayim] covers-you [tekassekka].

**22:12** Is-not God [eloah] [in the] height of-heaven [govah shamayim]? And-see [ure'eh] the-head [rosh] of-the-stars [kokhavim] — how high [ki ramu]!

**22:13** And-you-say [ve-amarta], 'What does-God [el] know [yada]? Through the-thick-cloud [ba'ad arafel] will-he-judge [yishpot]? **22:14** Clouds [avim] [are] a-covering [seter] for-him and-he-does-not see [velo yireh]; and-the-circuit [chug] of-the-heavens [shamayim] he-walks [yithalekh].'

**22:15** The-path [orach] of-old [olam] will-you-keep [ha-tishmor], which men [metei] of-wickedness [aven] have-trod [dareku]? **22:16** Who were-seized [qumetsu] before-their-time [velo et], [whose] foundation [yessodam] was-poured-out [yutsaq] [as] a-river [nahar]?

**22:17** Who-said [ha-omerim] to-God [la-el], 'Depart [sur] from-us'; and-'What can-Shaddai do [yif'al] to-them [lamo]?'

**22:18** Yet-he filled [mille] their-houses [batteihem] [with] good [tov] — but-the-counsel [va'atsat] of-the-wicked [reshaim] is-far [rachaqah] from-me.

**22:19** The-righteous [tsaddiqim] see [yir'u] and-are-glad [veyismachu], and-the-innocent [naqi] mocks [yil'ag] them [lamo]: **22:20** 'Surely [im lo] our-adversary [qimanu] is-cut-off [nikhchad], and-their-abundance [yitram] fire [esh] has-consumed [akhlah].'

**22:21** Acquaint-yourself [hasken] now with-him [immo] and-be-at-peace [ushelam]; by-these [bahem] good [tovah] will-come [tevo'atekha] to-you.

**22:22** Receive [qach] now from-his-mouth [mippiv] instruction [torah], and-set [vesim] his-words [amarav] in-your-heart [bilvavekha].

**22:23** If you-return [tashuv] to Shaddai, you-will-be-built-up [tibbane]; if-you-put-far [tarchiq] injustice [avlah] from-your-tent [me-aholekha].

**22:24** And-set [vesit] upon the-dust [al afar] [your] gold [betser], and-[the gold of] Ophir [ofir] among-the-rocks [betsur] of-the-streams [nechalim]; **22:25** and-Shaddai will-be your-gold [betsarekha], and-silver [kessef] of-strength [to'afot] for-you.

**22:26** For then upon Shaddai you-will-delight-yourself [tit'annag], and-you-will-lift [vetissa] to God [eloah] your-face [panekha].

**22:27** You-will-pray [ta'tir] to-him and-he-will-hear-you [veyishma'ekha], and-your-vows [underekha] you-will-pay [teshallem]. **22:28** And-you-will-decree [vetigzar] a-thing [omer] and-it-will-be-established [vayyaqam] for-you, and-upon your-ways [derakhekha] light [or] will-shine [nagah].

**22:29** When [they] bring-low [hishpilu] you-will-say [vetomer], 'Lifting-up! [gevah]'; and-the-lowly of-eyes [shach einayim] he-will-save [yoshia']. **22:30** He-will-deliver [yemallet] [even] the-not-innocent [i naqi]; and-he-is-delivered [venimlatah] by-the-cleanness [bevor] of-your-hands [kappekha]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**vv.6-9 — The specific accusations:** For the first time, Eliphaz makes concrete charges: Job stripped the naked, withheld food and water, sent away widows empty, crushed orphans. These accusations are fabricated — the reader knows from chapter 1 that Job was righteous. Eliphaz has moved from theological argument to slander.

**v.12 — "height of heaven":** Eliphaz turns Job's own argument against him. Job had appealed to God's cosmic sovereignty (ch. 12); Eliphaz now accuses Job of using God's transcendence as evidence that God cannot see human behavior.

**v.17 — "Depart from us":** Eliphaz quotes Job 21:14-15 back at him — the words of the wicked that Job cited. The implication: if you agree with the wicked's description of reality, you are one of them.

**v.30 — i naqi:** "The not-innocent" — a difficult phrase. Some emend *i* to *iy* ("island") and read "the island of the innocent." Others read it as "even one who is not innocent." The verse suggests that Job's restored righteousness could have intercessory power for others.

*— EMET*
